title: Where Do Ideas Come From?
description: Find problems worth solving. Your own pain points are your best ideas.

title: Validate Before Building
description: Talk to 5 potential users. Is this actually a problem?

title: Scope It Down
description: MVP mindset. What's the smallest version that solves the core problem?

title: Positioning Your Tool
description: What makes your tool different from the ten others like it.

title: Deciding Whether to Keep Building
description: The decision point between prototype and product.

title: Where Ideas Actually Come From
description: Generate tool ideas from friction you can actually observe — your own recurring annoyances, the workarounds other people build because a tool is missing, and the strained spreadsheets that are secretly running someone's business — instead of from brainstorming sessions that produce plausible-sounding nothing.

title: Finding Out Before You Build
description: Test whether an idea is actually wanted before spending weeks on it — asking about behaviour instead of intentions, taking the existing workaround seriously, running cheap signal tests, and killing an idea early when the evidence says to.

title: Cutting It Down to Shippable
description: Reduce a validated idea to the smallest version that's genuinely useful — the version that solves one job completely, the features that get cut versus the one that can't, and faking the hard part instead of building it.

title: Who It's For
description: Define a specific user well enough that design decisions become obvious — a real person's situation instead of 'everyone,' where those people actually spend their time, designing for someone with no energy today, and saying plainly who it isn't for.

title: What Already Exists
description: Find what's genuinely already out there before building — looking properly instead of assuming a gap, naming specifically why an existing tool falls short, taking free and open-source alternatives seriously as competition, and deciding honestly whether to build anyway, for a real reason or a rationalized one.
